title: Award Chart Sweet Spots: Where Your Points Buy the Most
summary: What award chart sweet spots are, why airline charts create them, which ones your Chase, Amex, Capital One, Citi or Bilt points reach, and why they vanish.
body_markdown:
On Alaska's Atmos Rewards chart, a business class seat on a partner airline from San Francisco to Hong Kong starts at 75,000 points. Leave from Los Angeles instead, a flight only about 330 miles longer, and the same seat starts at 85,000.


Same cabin, same destination. The price moved because of how the award chart is built. An **award chart** is the price list a loyalty program publishes in points instead of dollars, and an award chart sweet spot is a route or cabin where that price list charges far fewer points than the seat is worth.


Every program writes its own chart, so the same flight can be cheap in one program and expensive in the next. Charts also move. Air Canada's Aeroplan repriced on June 1, 2026, raising some prices and cutting others, so numbers quoted in older sweet spot lists often no longer book.


This guide covers why sweet spots exist, which ones your credit card points can reach today, why they disappear, and how to check one before you move a single point. For our ranked list of the best redemptions right now, see[the 12 best award flight deals for 2026](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/where-your-points-go-furthest-award-flight-deals) .


At Pointhound, we search 21 loyalty programs and 200+ airlines at once, which is exactly the comparison a sweet spot depends on.


## What Is an Award Chart Sweet Spot?


An award chart sweet spot is a route or cabin where a loyalty program charges far fewer points than the seat is worth.


It is always relative. Many seats can be booked through several programs, because airlines let each other's programs book their seats, and each program sets its own points price. The cheapest of those prices, set against the cash fare, is the sweet spot. That is why Pointhound compares programs side by side instead of one at a time.


Most sweet spots are not mistakes. They come from choices a program made on purpose: pricing by distance, pricing a whole region at one flat rate, or discounting its own planes. Every one of those choices leaves some routes much cheaper than others.


Two words on many charts matter more than they look: *starting at* . A starting price is the lowest a program will charge, not a guarantee. Alaska, for example, notes that actual prices "may vary based on route-specific factors, including city pair combinations, partner airline pricing, market demand" ([Alaska Airlines](https://www.alaskaair.com/atmosrewards/content/use-points/award-charts) ).


So a sweet spot tells you where to look. It does not tell you a seat is open on your date.


## Why Do Award Charts Have Sweet Spots?


Award charts have sweet spots because programs price by distance, by zone or through sales, and each method makes some routes far cheaper.


Most sweet spots you will read about trace back to one of four patterns. Learn to spot the pattern and you can find new sweet spots yourself, instead of waiting for someone else's list.


Pattern How the program prices Where the sweet spot hides Example


Distance-based chart By miles flown, in bands Flights just under a band limit Atmos: Americas flights under 700 miles from 4,500 points


Zone-based chart One flat price for a whole region The longest flight inside the zone Turkish: nonstop U.S. domestic partner flights at 22,500 in business


Airline's own sale price Discounts on its own planes The airline's own routes Virgin Atlantic: London-New York from 6,000


Monthly promotion Rotating discounts That month's routes Flying Blue: up to 25% off, new each month


### Distance-based charts make short flights cheap


Atmos Rewards prices partner flights by distance, in ranges called bands. In the Americas, a flight under 700 miles starts at **4,500 points** in economy, and the top band, 6,001 miles and above, starts at 30,000 in economy and 60,000 in business. Taxes and a $20 partner award fee per person, each way, come on top ([Alaska Airlines](https://www.alaskaair.com/atmosrewards/content/use-points/award-charts) ).


The value sits just under the top of each band. San Francisco to Hong Kong is about 6,900 miles, just under the 7,000-mile line, so Atmos business class starts at 75,000. Los Angeles to Hong Kong, about 7,250 miles, falls in the next band up and starts at 85,000.


On a distance chart, always check whether a nearby airport keeps you under the next band. That habit matters most in[business class](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/how-to-find-cheap-business-class-flights-with-points) , where one band can mean 10,000 points or more.


### Zone-based charts make long flights inside one zone cheap


Turkish Airlines Miles&Smiles does the opposite. It charges one flat price for nonstop partner flights within a single country: **15,000 miles** in economy and 22,500 in business, one way ([Turkish Airlines](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/miles-and-smiles/redeem-miles/redeem-miles-on-flights/turkish-airlines-award-tickets/) ).


That means a nonstop coast-to-coast flight on United, one of the longest flights in the lower 48, costs the same miles as a short hop. The flat price rewards you for flying as far as the zone allows.


Hawaii gets its own price on Turkish: 25,000 miles in economy and 40,000 in business each way on nonstop partner flights (same[Turkish Airlines](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/miles-and-smiles/redeem-miles/redeem-miles-on-flights/turkish-airlines-award-tickets/) chart). If Hawaii is the goal, our[guide to flying to Hawaii with points](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/how-to-fly-to-hawaii-with-points) covers the other routes in.


The catch with any partner chart is availability. Turkish can only sell the United seats United releases to partners.


### Airlines discount their own flights


An airline controls its own seats, so its own program can set special low prices on them. Virgin Atlantic's Saver reward seats between London and New York start at **6,000 points** in economy, 10,500 in premium economy, and 29,000 in Upper Class, its lie-flat business cabin, one way, plus taxes, fees and charges ([Virgin Atlantic](https://www.virginatlantic.com/en-US/flying-club/spend-points/reward-seats/saver-reward-seats) ).


Saver is Virgin's label for its lowest reward price, and it shows up on thousands of flights, not every flight. London to Miami and London to Orlando start slightly higher, at 7,500 points in economy.


When you are looking at a trip to[Europe with points](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/how-to-fly-to-europe-with-points-complete-guide) , check the operating airline's own program first. It can be the cheapest way to book its own plane.


### Monthly promotions rotate the cheap routes


Air France-KLM's Flying Blue releases new Promo rewards on the first day of every month, at up to 25% off the usual price. Each month's batch has its own travel window (September's runs to February 28, 2027), and long-haul Promo rewards cover Air France and KLM flights to and from Europe ([Flying Blue](https://www.flyingblue.us/en/flights/promo-rewards) ).


These are real discounts, but they expire. Check the current month's list on the day you plan to book, never last month's.


## Which Award Chart Sweet Spots Can Your Points Reach?


Bilt points reach every sweet spot in this guide, and Bilt is the only one of the five major card programs that transfers to Atmos Rewards. Virgin Atlantic and Flying Blue are the two programs here that all five reach.


A sweet spot only helps if your points can get there. Here is each sweet spot above, mapped against the five major transferable points currencies.


Sweet spot Program Price from, one way Chase Amex Capital One Citi Bilt


Partner flights under 700 miles in the Americas Atmos Rewards 4,500 economy - - - - Yes


U.S. to Asia partner business class, 5,001-7,000 miles Atmos Rewards 75,000 business - - - - Yes


Nonstop U.S. domestic partner flights outside Hawaii, any length Turkish Miles&Smiles 15,000 economy, 22,500 business - - Yes Yes Yes


U.S. mainland to Hawaii on partners Turkish Miles&Smiles 25,000 economy, 40,000 business - - Yes Yes Yes


London-New York Saver seats Virgin Atlantic Flying Club 6,000 economy, 29,000 Upper Class Yes Yes Yes, via Virgin Red Yes Yes


Monthly Promo rewards to and from Europe Air France-KLM Flying Blue Up to 25% off Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes


Transfer partners come from each program's own published list:[Chase](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/how-to-transfer-chase-ultimate-rewards-points) ,[Capital One](https://www.capitalone.com/learn-grow/money-management/venture-miles-transfer-partnerships/) ,[Citi](https://www.citi.com/credit-cards/money-management/citi-thankyou-rewards-faqs) and[Bilt](https://support.biltrewards.com/hc/en-us/articles/19086448638989-Bilt-s-Transfer-Partners) . Amex partners are from[NerdWallet's transfer partner chart](https://www.nerdwallet.com/travel/learn/heres-how-you-can-transfer-your-points-from-any-major-credit-card-issuer) , updated July 2026.


A few things the table does not show at a glance:


- **Capital One** reaches Turkish, Virgin Atlantic and Flying Blue. Its Virgin partner is called Virgin Red, which turns Capital One miles into Virgin Points, the same points Virgin Atlantic uses for reward seats ([Virgin Red](https://www.virgin.com/en-us/virgin-red/capital-one) ).
- **Chase and Amex** both reach Virgin Atlantic and Flying Blue, but neither reaches Turkish or Atmos Rewards.
- **Citi** reaches Turkish, Virgin Atlantic and Flying Blue, though the value of each transfer depends on which Citi card you hold ([Citi](https://www.citi.com/credit-cards/money-management/citi-thankyou-rewards-faqs) ).


For every airline each program reaches, not only the ones above, see our[full guide to transferring credit card points to airlines](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/how-to-transfer-credit-card-points-to-airlines) .


## Why Do Sweet Spots Disappear?


Sweet spots disappear when a program rewrites its award chart, and programs can change prices with little notice.


Aeroplan is this year's clearest example. On June 1, 2026, Air Canada changed its chart with "a combination of increases and decreases," applying to tickets booked or reissued on or after that date ([Air Canada](https://www.aircanada.com/ca/en/aco/home/aeroplan/news/2026-an-update-on-the-aeroplan-flight-reward-chart.html) ).


Some changes were small. Business class between North America and Europe on flights of 4,001 to 6,000 miles rose from 70,000 to 75,000 points. Others were not. Aeroplan puts Europe, Africa, the Middle East and India in one Atlantic zone, and Asia, Australia and New Zealand in a Pacific zone. On flights over 7,000 miles between those two zones, business class on Air Canada and select partners jumped from **60,000 to 100,000 points** . A sweet spot that existed on May 31 cost 40,000 more points the next day.


The same update also created cheaper prices. Business class within the Atlantic zone on flights of 2,001 to 4,000 miles fell from 45,000 to 40,000 points, and business class within the Pacific zone on flights over 7,000 miles fell from 90,000 to 85,000 (same[Air Canada](https://www.aircanada.com/ca/en/aco/home/aeroplan/news/2026-an-update-on-the-aeroplan-flight-reward-chart.html) update). Sweet spots do not only vanish. They move, and the new ones reward whoever checks first.


Three habits protect you from a sweet spot that vanishes:


1. **Check the chart on the program's own site the day you book.** Not a list, not a forum post, not last month's article.
2. **Keep points in your card program until you find a seat.** Transferable points can still go to any of your card's partners. Airline miles are stuck with one airline's next price change.
3. **Transfer only after you have found the seat.** As Chase puts it, "point transfers to travel partners are final" ([Chase](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/how-to-transfer-chase-ultimate-rewards-points) ).


## How to Check a Sweet Spot Before You Transfer


Checking a sweet spot takes five steps, and the order matters because the last one cannot be undone.


1. **Confirm the price on the program's own site.** Charts change, and the program's page is the only source that counts.
2. **Confirm your points can reach it.** Use the table above, or our transfer partner guide for everything else.
3. **Find an open seat.** A chart lists prices, not seats. This is the easiest step to skip, and skipping it is how points end up stuck in the wrong program.
4. **Compare the points price with the cash fare** for the same flight. If the cash fare is low, save your points.
5. **Transfer, then book directly with the airline.** Most transfers are instant, though a few take several days, so book as soon as the points arrive.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Do award chart sweet spots still exist in 2026?


Yes. Charts do change, as Aeroplan's did on June 1, but distance-based, zone-based, sale and promotional pricing still leave cheap routes. Virgin Atlantic Saver seats between London and New York start at 6,000 points in economy, and Atmos Rewards partner flights under 700 miles in the Americas start at 4,500. Always confirm the current price first.


### Which credit card points reach the most sweet spots?


Of the sweet spots in this guide, Bilt reaches all of them and is the only one of the five major programs that transfers to Atmos Rewards. Virgin Atlantic and Flying Blue are reachable from all five, Capital One through its Virgin Red partnership. Capital One and Citi also reach Turkish Miles&Smiles, while Chase and Amex do not.


### What does "starting at" mean on an award chart?


It is the lowest price a program publishes for that route, cabin and distance, not a promise. The actual price can be higher depending on the route, the partner airline and demand, and a seat has to be open at that price. Treat a starting price as where to look, not what you will pay.


### Are award chart sweet spots only worth it for business class?


No. Premium cabins show the largest gaps between points and cash, but economy sweet spots are real too. Virgin Atlantic prices London to New York from 6,000 points in economy, and Turkish Miles&Smiles prices any nonstop U.S. domestic partner flight outside Hawaii at 15,000 miles in economy, however long the flight.


### How often do airline award charts change?


There is no fixed schedule. Programs often change charts when their costs change, sometimes with both increases and decreases at once, as Aeroplan did on June 1, 2026. Monthly promotions like Flying Blue's change every month by design. Check the program's own chart on the day you book.


## Key Takeaways


- An award chart sweet spot is a route or cabin where a loyalty program charges far fewer points than the seat is worth, and it only shows up when you compare programs.
- Most sweet spots come from one of four patterns: distance-based charts, zone-based charts, an airline's own sale prices, or monthly promotions.
- On distance charts, the value sits just under a band limit. San Francisco to Hong Kong starts at 75,000 Atmos points in business, Los Angeles to Hong Kong at 85,000.
- Bilt reaches every sweet spot in this guide and is the only major card program that transfers to Atmos Rewards. All five major programs reach Virgin Atlantic and Flying Blue.
- Charts can change with little notice. Aeroplan's June 1, 2026 update moved one business class price from 60,000 to 100,000 points.
- Transfers are final, so confirm the price and an open seat before you move any points.


## A Sweet Spot Is Only Half the Answer


The chart tells you where points go furthest. It does not tell you whether a seat is open, or which of your programs can book it today. That second half is the part that turns a sweet spot into a trip.
